data.title: Process Hollowing
data.summary: The sample launches a legitimate process in a suspended state, unmaps its original image, and writes its own payload into the vacated memory before resuming it — running under that process's identity.
data.description:
Hollowing is attractive specifically because the resulting process is, by every external
measure, the legitimate binary: its path, signature metadata and parent process all read
as expected, and tools that trust a process based on its image path alone will trust the
hollowed one too. The giveaway lives in memory layout, not on disk — the mapped image no
longer matches the on-disk file at that path once unmapping and remapping have occurred.
data.recommendation:
* Alert on NtUnmapViewOfSection targeting a process's own main module, immediately followed by a write into that region — this sequence has very few legitimate uses.
* Compare a running process's mapped image against the on-disk file at its reported path; a mismatch is a strong hollowing indicator.
* Prefer process-creation telemetry (parent/child, command line) over path-based trust alone when triaging a process this technique could have hollowed.
data.short_recommendation: Alert on NtUnmapViewOfSection against a process's own module followed by a write into that region.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Created a suspended svchost.exe, unmapped its main module, and wrote the payload image into the vacated region before resuming the thread.

mbc_techniques.implementation: NtUnmapViewOfSection followed by WriteProcessMemory into a suspended child process before resuming it.
